rule: Release the issue's claim (restore the trigger label or move it to a visible blocked state) whenever a runner parks work without running it, and make the parked comment describe what actually re-triggers the work.
why: A parked issue stayed claimed with its trigger label removed and no sweep re-listed it, so it would never run even though the comment promised it would.

rule: Validate owner/repo and issue numbers parsed from issue bodies against a strict allowlist pattern, rejecting '.' and '..' segments, before interpolating them into any gh api path.
why: Unvalidated body-derived refs such as '../..#5' let an untrusted issue author redirect authenticated API calls to other endpoints or repositories.

rule: Memoize dependency-graph traversals per node with visited/visiting marking, and enforce depth, node, and concurrency caps that fail closed when exceeded.
why: Per-path recursion over author-linked issues reached roughly 10^11 paths, which would hang the gate while the issue stayed claimed.

rule: Apply the readiness gate on every path that can start work, including spec-advanced and carried-over issue ids, not only the primary listing.
why: A blocked issue was specced, parked, and then re-added from the spec-advanced carry-over and built anyway, because that path skipped the gate.

rule: Only let trusted root-issue data produce invalid, error, or failed results; content from other issue bodies must be ignored or treated as a leaf.
why: Any outside author who edits a dependency body could park trusted issues in needs-info or turn the scheduled sweep red with a non-zero exit.

rule: Track visited dependency nodes by identity and count distinct issues against the walk cap, so shared nodes are not refetched or double-counted.
why: Diamond-shaped dependency graphs were refetched and counted as extra visits, tripping the node cap and sending valid chains to needs-info.

rule: Do not edit files under .github/workflows or templates/github to wire new secrets or env; describe the exact edit (declare the secret in workflow_call.secrets, map it into the step env, update the callers) in the PR body for a human to appl…
why: The App credential shipped unreachable because the reusable workflows never declared or mapped its secrets, and the PR body omitted the hand edits that CLAUDE.md requires.

rule: When a preferred credential fails to mint, fall back to the next configured credential inside the resolver, and derive any logged credential label from the credential actually used.
why: A failed App mint silently dropped to the ambient GITHUB_TOKEN, so factory PRs got no CI while the logs still claimed the App token.

rule: Request only the GitHub App permissions the code actually uses, and keep the documented permission list identical to the permissions constant in code.
why: An unused issues:write scope made minting fail for Apps without Issues access and contradicted both the docs and the stated least-privilege intent.

rule: When a function gains a default that makes network or container calls, inject a stub for that dependency or disable its switch in the shared test options for every existing test that reaches that function.
why: Existing doctor tests reached the real npm registry because they did not stub the new default, so the suite became network-dependent and could time out on slow links.

rule: Throw on non-OK upstream responses instead of resolving to undefined, and never cache a failure result as if it were a successful lookup.
why: A single transient registry error resolved to undefined and was stored for the full cache TTL, so the hub kept reporting a lookup failure for an hour.

rule: Use `Refs #N` instead of `Closes #N` in the PR body whenever the PR does not deliver every item the linked issue or PR title names, such as a UI or action.
why: Using `Closes` would auto-close the issue even though the headline Update button and its UI were missing from the diff.

rule: Run `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and the affected tests locally before pushing, and delete any helper or variable the change no longer uses.
why: An unused test helper failed `pnpm lint`, which CI's `pnpm verify` runs, so the PR was blocked on a gate the author could have run locally.

rule: Substitute or remove every placeholder token (such as `YOUR_APP_SLUG`) in generated templates, and add a test that fails if any placeholder survives `apply`.
why: An unreplaced `YOUR_APP_SLUG[bot]` shipped as a live entry in every generated revise gate, and the existing test only checked the `YOUR_LOGIN` placeholder, so nothing caught it.

rule: Verify a test's or comment's premise against the base branch's current workflow files before asserting it, and state the real constraint (such as a lagging `@v1` tag) in the comment.
why: A new test asserted that no reusable workflow declared the App secret, but the base branch already declared and mapped it, so the test blocked the template change that would have made the feature work.

rule: Normalise CRLF to LF on both the pasted PR-body text and the manifest string before any substring comparison against human-edited content.
why: Browser-edited PR bodies use CRLF while manifest JSON uses LF, so multi-line items never match and a correctly pasted item stays missing forever.

rule: Escape or defang any manifest- or agent-supplied text before embedding it in a generated PR-body block, and locate block boundaries with markers that such text cannot reproduce.
why: Unescaped ids and descriptions let a reporter forge the human-paste boundary, so a block could be marked discharged with nothing pasted.

rule: Run PR-body state updates before any early return that skips the push, not only on the pushed-commit path.
why: Discharge ran only after a pushed commit, so a human who pasted the fix with no other code feedback never saw the disclosure update.

rule: When concatenating per-repository results into one combined list, sort the merged list by its timestamp (newest first) before returning it, and add a test that uses at least two repositories.
why: Each repository's results were appended in config order, so the newest run from a later repository was buried below older runs from an earlier one.

rule: Do not add a source file whose name differs from an existing file only by letter case, and check for case-only collisions before creating any new module.
why: A case-only duplicate (RepoFilter.tsx beside repoFilter.ts) resolves to different files on case-insensitive macOS and case-sensitive Linux, so it breaks on one platform while CI stays green.

rule: When one operation fans out across repositories, enforce a shared budget for expensive calls such as comment fetches and external CLI invocations across the whole fan-out, not a separate limit per repository.
why: A per-repository cap multiplied by the repository count produced roughly 16 concurrent gh processes on every refresh, exhausting the API quota the factory shares.
